metric: three independently checkable properties of a copied home: (a) no credential travels, (b) no bin/cli entry names the source home, (c) the copy is usable on another platform

a_no_credential_travels.note: a raw copy applies no product logic, so this is a property of `home clone` -- the copier an image build is told to use

b_no_shim_names_the_source_home.note: read off the RAW copy: a frozen absolute path is what a raw copy carries, and it is not a dangling reference so nothing else reports it

c_usable_on_another_platform.note: pm/ is deliberately not skipped, so the bytes travel; each version directory must be stamped with the platform that provisioned it

method: shutil.copytree(symlinks=True) -- cp -R, the way a Dockerfile COPY works, never `home clone`, whose exclusions and re-anchoring are exactly what an image build does NOT get
